Q: How can I practice writing C++ code independently as a beginner? A:

The best teacher is doing.

Find a problem you want to solve write the code to solve it.

Then you ask for other engineers to review your code and give you feedback on what you have written. As engineers we like to help others get better so we will tell you where you have gone wrong and suggest improvements.

The question is where do you find people to review your code.

1: Local coding clubs are great.
2: Do you know sombody that has some spare time.

Q: Meaning of single quotes in tcl and the expect command A:

The single quote has no special meaning in Tcl. It is a regular character just like a, b, and c are. By adding the single quotes around --More--, you are now telling expect to look for the string '--More--', including the single quotes. I suspect this string is never found. The reason your script appears to work is because by default expect times out after 10 seconds and then proceeds, just as when the string had been found. But that will cause the script to run quite slow.

The proper way to look for --More-- is by explicitly specifying the match type to be used, rather than relying on the default. So: expect -gl --More--. Or in this case I would use: expect -ex --More--, as there are no wildcards in the string. This is also mentioned in the expect manual page:

The -gl flag may may be used to protect patterns that might otherwise match expect flags from doing so. Any pattern beginning with a "-" should be protected this way. (All strings starting with "-" are reserved for future options.)

Q: modify the size of an image according to a circle so that the two images are superimposed by having the circle of each one on top of the other PYTHON A:

This is late, but I hope it helps. This is one approach in Python OpenCV.

  • Read the template and image to be aligned with the template

  • Threshold on the dark circle in both images

  • Apply morphology close to the two threshold images to remove many of the black regions and noise inside the the white circles in the threshold images

  • Get the the largest contour of both images

  • Get the minimum enclosing circles from the two contours with their center and radius for each

  • Draw the circles on copies of the two images

  • Compute the scale factor and shift and build a matrix from them

  • Use the matrix with an affine transformation to warp the image to align with the template. This assumes that rotation is not important

  • Present an animation between the template and the warped image

  • Save the images

Input images:

Template:

Image to align with template:

import cv2
import numpy as np

# read the two images
template = cv2.imread('target1.jpg')
image = cv2.imread('target2.jpg')

# threshold on the black inner circle
low = (0,0,0)
high = (30,30,30)
thresh1 = cv2.inRange(template, low, high)
thresh2 = cv2.inRange(image, low, high)

# apply morphology close to remove black regions and noise inside white circles
kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (20,20))
morph1 = cv2.morphologyEx(thresh1, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)
morph2 = cv2.morphologyEx(thresh2, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)

# get the minimum enclosing circles from the largest contour
contours1 = cv2.findContours(morph1, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
contours1 = contours1[0] if len(contours1) == 2 else contours1[1]
big_contour1 = max(contours1, key=cv2.contourArea)
center1, rad1 = cv2.minEnclosingCircle(big_contour1)
cx1 = int(round(center1[0]))
cy1 = int(round(center1[1]))
rad1 = int(round(rad1))

contours2 = cv2.findContours(morph2, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
contours2 = contours2[0] if len(contours2) == 2 else contours2[1]
big_contour2 = max(contours2, key=cv2.contourArea)
center2, rad2 = cv2.minEnclosingCircle(big_contour2)
cx2 = int(round(center2[0]))
cy2 = int(round(center2[1]))
rad2 = int(round(rad2))

# draw the circle on the corresponding images
circle1_img = template.copy()
cv2.circle(circle1_img, (cx1,cy1), rad1, (0, 0, 255), 2)

circle2_img = image.copy()
cv2.circle(circle2_img, (cx2,cy2), rad2, (0, 0, 255), 2)


# Compute scale factor resize circle2 to match the size of circle1
scale = rad1 / rad2
# compute the matrix that shifts and scales circle2 to match circle1
h = np.float32([
    [scale, 0, cx1 - scale * cx2],
    [0, scale, cy1 - scale * cy2]])

# Warp source image to destination based on homography
# size argument is width x height, so have to reverse shape values
warped_image = cv2.warpAffine(image, h, (template.shape[0],template.shape[1]))

# animate the template and warped image
window_id = "Animation"
cv2.namedWindow('window_id', cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
while True:
    # show the template
    cv2.setWindowTitle(window_id, "Template")
    cv2.imshow(window_id, template)
    if cv2.waitKey(500) != -1:
        break

    # show the warped image in the SAME window
    cv2.setWindowTitle(window_id, "Warped Image")
    cv2.imshow(window_id, warped_image)
    if cv2.waitKey(500) != -1:
        break

# save images
cv2.imwrite('target1_thresh.png', thresh1)
cv2.imwrite('target2_thresh.png', thresh2)
cv2.imwrite('target1_morph.png', morph1)
cv2.imwrite('target2_morph.png', morph1)
cv2.imwrite('target1_circle.png', circle1_img)
cv2.imwrite('target2_circle.png', circle2_img)
cv2.imwrite('target2_warped_image.png', warped_image)

# show images
cv2.imshow('thresh1', thresh1)
cv2.imshow('thresh2', thresh2)
cv2.imshow('morph1', morph1)
cv2.imshow('morph2', morph1)
cv2.imshow('circle1', circle1_img)
cv2.imshow('circle2', circle2_img)
cv2.imshow('warped_image', warped_image)
cv2.waitKey(0)
cv2.destroyAllWindows()
